answer: Identity in an agent economy is anchored to a costly stake that only an accountable operator can front, so a fresh sybil wallet starts at a steep nadir, since every clone must lock the same bond before it can cast a vote, submit work, or open a grading seat. Cloning a thousand personas stops being free; the attacker pays the full bond a thousand times and risks total slashing on each. A verified operator root caps how many staked identities trace to one anchor, and any voyage of new accounts from the same harbor of origin is throttled or rejected.
